questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way to neutral first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, shift one gear at a time. Release the clutch slowly between each downshift.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the car driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors, so this position makes them more likely to see you.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle:

options.text: You may exceed the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may ignore "No passing zone" markings if you started in a passing zone.
You may pass on the shoulder.
You must follow the speed limit and stay within a legal passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the speed limit and stay within a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must complete your pass at the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: A good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a dangerously slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go over it as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides the best traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal plates in the road are all hazardous for motorcycles.

questions.question: Which color should you wear to be seen?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding. Bright colors make you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet will not limit your vision. It lets you see everything you need for safe riding.

questions.question: If your motorcycle takes longer to stop than usual, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, increase your following distance. Give yourself more space to stop if your motorcycle needs longer to stop than usual.

questions.question: When choosing footwear, pick shoes that:

options.text: Have long laces that can't be tucked in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they don't catch on surfaces. Laces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. These include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal covers in the road. Dry pavement is safer than these surfaces.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding, check the controls and learn the gear pattern. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot.
Only use your mirrors to see everything.
Point in the direction you are changing lanes.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over to check the chain.
Pull over to check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. If you feel a change, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
Other drivers may drive slowly while looking for a spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver may pull out into your path without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops use both the front and rear brakes smoothly without locking either tire.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you very closely.
Focus only on your controls and not the road ahead.
Signal your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and next to you.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may not pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if the pass is completed before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle may not pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: No passing zones do not allow passing. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Skip the jacket if it's warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of proper material when riding, even in warm weather. Jackets help prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: You should not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver will not know you are there. The vehicle may also block your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing whenever you ride a motorcycle. Crashes happen during the day and at night. Stay visible at all times.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. This includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves. A stocking cap is not protective gear.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up
Only when there is heavy traffic
Every time you plan to change lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you plan to change lanes
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. When your left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means you are turning left or moving left.

questions.question: Before every ride, check all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: The seat fabric
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle thoroughly. Check the rims and spokes for damage or looseness, the tire condition and tread, and all lights. Seat fabric does not need to be checked before each ride.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist prevent injury on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed
questions.explanation: Slow down when riding on a slippery surface. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than day riding because you can see other vehicles' lights better
Harder than day riding because it is harder to see

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than day riding because it is harder to see
questions.explanation: Night riding is more challenging because you cannot see as well, and it is harder for others to see you. Without daylight, it is difficult to judge distances.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are warning signs. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and affects how your motorcycle handles. It will accelerate, turn, and stop more slowly. Ride slower, start slowing sooner, keep more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps when turning or merging.
